Move shares the same stationary tread/rock vocabulary as the other pets. Several Greet/Play phases extend the pink snout/mouth mark as a narrow strip below the face, making the intended expression ambiguous.
Feet remain thin colored strokes and can merge with nearby mass; no unmistakable lost source organ was established.

defects.detail: MOVE around0.5–1.0s merges gray lower-body/limb pixels into a broad flat rectangular shelf, making separate leg articulation hard to read. This is visible silhouette merging, not a claim that numerical joints detach.

In GREET around0.25s and1.25s, the pink snout/mouth mark elongates into a narrow strip below the face; the result reads ambiguously as a dangling tongue/facial mark rather than a clearly articulated mouth.
Several GREET phases stretch the pink facial mark vertically below the head, making the intended mouth expression unclear despite the main head/body carrier remaining coherent.

limitations: This is actual agent visual review of40 PNG sheets, not a human review. Each sheet has four action rows and eight phase images, giving1280 inspected rendered frames.
Only developmental day75 is pictured. Supplemental numerical motion checks at ages30/75/120 cover7680 frames separately and do not increase this visual-review count.
Eight static phases at0,.25,.5,.75,1,1.25,1.5,1.75 seconds cannot establish continuous-time smoothness, behavior between samples or a complete animation loop.

Idle and settled Play often look almost frozen at sheet scale. No clear blink interval is captured, but the short window does not cover a full blink cycle; this is not evidence that blinking is broken or absent.
The supplied Play target is(48,38), but no target marker, ball, grasped object or contact indicator is drawn in these PNGs. Successful catch/contact cannot be visually confirmed.
Small feature aliases/overlaps are recorded as readability alerts. Mathematical joint separation or definite source-organ loss is not inferred from ambiguous underpainting alone.
These extra motion receipts are separate from primary lifecycle/overview review coverage.
